key_insight: AI can support nearly every stage of the ARPES workflow, from sample preparation and acquisition to analysis and theory comparison, but the field still lacks standardized large-scale datasets and mature validation.
engineering_relevance: For materials and condensed matter labs, this points to AI-enabled automation that can improve throughput, reduce manual effort, and move ARPES toward more reproducible, self-driving experiments.
method: Review ML methods relevant to experimental condensed matter physics
Map AI use cases across the full ARPES workflow
Discuss a six-level framework for laboratory automation
evidence_signal: The paper is a review rather than a new benchmark study, and it notes that ARPES data remain small and fragmented compared with large shared datasets like ImageNet.
watch_item: Pretrained models may transfer well only if dataset standards, task definitions, and validation protocols are made consistent across laboratories.
paper_title: Progress and Prospect of AI in ARPES Workflow
